uncited: This family extends 3D Gaussian Splatting by attaching high-dimensional semantic or language feature vectors to each Gaussian, enabling open-vocabulary segmentation, phrase grounding, and visual question answering via real-time alpha-blended feature maps.

It differs from sibling methods by prioritizing semantic understanding over geometric fidelity or appearance; while [3D Gaussian Splatting MVP](3410-3d-gaussian-splatting-mvp.md) focuses on minimal viable rendering and [Analytic-Splatting](8084-analytic-splatting.md) on mathematical precision, this approach leverages the rasterizer as a feature distillation pipeline for vision-language models.

The core mechanism involves storing a feature vector $\mathbf{f}_i$ (of dimension $D$, typically 512 or 768) alongside the standard Gaussian parameters (position $\mathbf{x}_i$, covariance $\Sigma_i$, opacity $\alpha_i$, spherical harmonics coefficients) for each Gaussian $i$.

During rendering, these features are accumulated per pixel using alpha-blending, producing a 2D feature map $\mathbf{F}(p)$ that can be compared against text embeddings or decoded by a segmentation head.
- $\mathcal{O}$ is the set of Gaussians sorted by depth (front-to-back) that overlap pixel $p$.
- $\mathbf{f}_i$ is the feature vector of Gaussian $i$.
- The term $\prod_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - \alpha_j)$ represents the accumulated transparency from all Gaussians $j$ rendered before $i$ in the sorted order.
The resulting $\mathbf{F}(p)$ is a vector in $\mathbb{R}^D$.
The concept of attaching semantic features to 3D Gaussians emerged as a natural extension of 3D Gaussian Splatting's ability to render high-dimensional data.

The feature blending formula is identical to the color blending in standard 3D Gaussian Splatting [S2, unofficial]:

The evidence states that the feature blending formula uses alpha-blending (F(p) = ∑ f_i α_i ∏ (1 - α_j)). However, standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) typically uses a different compositing formula for color, which is C(p) = ∑ c_i α_i ∏_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - α_j). While the mathematical structure appears similar, the claim that the formula is 'identical' is misleading because standard 3DGS does not blend high-dimensional feature vectors f_i in its standard color rendering pipeline; it blends colors c_i. Furthermore, the evidence does not explicitly compare the feature blending formula to the standard 3DGS color blending formula to assert identity, nor does it define the standard 3DGS color blending formula within the text to allow for a direct comparison of 'identity'. The evidence describes feature blending as a specific extension for vision-language tasks, not as an identical replication of the standard color blending mechanism.
